overview: Kenya is one of Africa's deepest women's health innovation ecosystems, anchored in Nairobi and spanning maternal and newborn health, sexual and reproductive health, menstrual health, telehealth and diagnostics. Kasha, a Kenya-based women's health e-commerce platform, raised the largest round ever by a woman-led African health startup, and Jacaranda Health's PROMPTS has reached nearly three million mothers by SMS. In 2025 Nairobi cemented its role as a continental hub, with UNFPA launching its global WomenX Collective Nairobi Hub and Sweden's DAYA venture studio opening an East Africa femtech accelerator there.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent activity centres on Nairobi becoming a hub for women's health innovation plus continued AI-driven maternal health scaling.

items.text: UNFPA, Government of Kenya, Africa CDC and Aga Khan University launch the global WomenX Collective Nairobi Hub, aiming to mobilise USD 100M in catalytic investment by 2030.
Sweden's DAYA venture studio opens its first East Africa hub in Nairobi, launching the region's first femtech accelerator for women-led ventures.
UNICEF Femtech Ventures announces its first cohort of 11 startups (from 1,100+ applications), including Kenya's SafeRide by Esheria, each receiving up to USD 100k equity-free.
Jacaranda Health and IDRC launch a partnership to scale responsible AI (a Swahili LLM in PROMPTS) for new and expecting mothers; PROMPTS has reached about 2.9M women.
The m-mama community emergency transport system (Vodafone Foundation, M-Pesa Foundation, USAID, government) becomes fully operational, benefiting 1.5M+ mothers.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Kenya has built a layered policy stack for reproductive health and digital health, including binding digital health legislation.

items.text: National Reproductive Health Policy 2022-2032 adopted, setting a decade-long framework for reproductive health services.
Digital Health Act 2023 enacted, establishing the Digital Health Agency and a Comprehensive Integrated Digital Health Information System.
Kenya RMNCAH-N Investment Case 2025/26-2029/30 published, mapping universal access to reproductive, maternal, newborn and adolescent health with nutrition.
National Family Planning Guidelines 7th Edition (2025) signed by the Ministry of Health.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Accelerators, hubs and outcome-based finance are concentrating in Nairobi.

items.text: WomenX Collective Nairobi Hub extends UNFPA's global network (after Berlin 2024), targeting 10.4M averted unintended pregnancies and 21,000 maternal lives saved by 2030.
DAYA Hub Africa launches East Africa's first femtech accelerator, with 100+ founder and partner registrations at launch.
A Grand Challenges grant supports advancing Kenya's women's health through policy and fem-tech capacity building.
Villgro Africa's African Women Innovating in Healthcare (AWIIH) 2025 cohort backs women-led health ventures across the region.
Tiko (Triggerise) runs a USD 10.1M Adolescent SRH Development Impact Bond, an outcome-based finance model reaching hundreds of thousands of adolescent girls.
